options: Enterprise Resource Planning
Electronic Record Processing
Enterprise Reporting Platform
External Resource Provisioning
questions.explain: ERP stands for Enterprise Resource Planning — one connected system running a company's core business processes.

questions.q: In the Blue Harbor Manufacturing example, what caused the warehouse to sell inventory that was already promised to another customer?
options: A bug in the ERP system
Disconnected spreadsheets that weren't updated in time
Too many employees using the same system
The customer canceled their order
questions.explain: Before ERP, sales and the warehouse each kept their own spreadsheet, so inventory promises made in one weren't reflected in the other in time.

options: A backup copy of company data kept offsite
A spreadsheet used only by the accounting department
The single authoritative source for a piece of business data
The name of Oracle's cloud data center
questions.explain: The system of record is the one place a transaction's details are considered authoritative — if the ERP says a customer owes $4,200, that is the number the company uses.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT listed as a real business reason companies adopt ERP?
options: Eliminating duplicate data entry
Standardizing processes across departments
Supporting audits with a defensible trail
Making the company's logo look more modern
questions.explain: ERP adoption is driven by eliminating duplicate entry, a single accurate picture of the business, standardized processes, audit support, and scalability — not branding.

questions.q: What is a 'module' in an ERP system?
options: One functional piece of the ERP, such as Financials or Procurement, that is integrated with the others
A training class new employees must complete
A separate company that competes with the ERP vendor
A type of spreadsheet used before ERP adoption
questions.explain: An ERP is a family of connected modules — Financials, Procurement, Supply Chain, HR, and others — that share data automatically rather than running as isolated tools.
